title: Imperative form (命令形) "Do!"
meaning: Blunt command. Used by superiors to subordinates, in emergencies, cheering, signs, and quoting instructions.
simpleExplanation: The imperative is the blunt command form: 書け！ (Write!), 食べろ！ (Eat!), しろ！ (Do it!). It is short, strong and rough. In everyday polite life you rarely say it to someone's face, but you meet it constantly: on signs (止まれ), in cheering (頑張れ！), in emergencies (逃げろ！) and when quoting what someone ordered (「静かにしろ」と言われた).
whenUsed: Superiors to subordinates in rough speech, parents to children, coaches and fans at sports events, emergency warnings, traffic signs, and reported commands (〜と言われた / と書いてある). Men use it more than women in casual speech.
formation: Group 1: change the last う-row sound to the え-row: 書く→書け, 行く→行け, 急ぐ→急げ, 待つ→待て, 飲む→飲め
Group 2: drop る and add ろ: 食べる→食べろ, 見る→見ろ, 起きる→起きろ
Group 3: する→しろ, 来る→来い (こい)
Irregular: くれる→くれ (貸してくれ = lend it to me)

diagram.root: 書く / 食べる / する / 来る

examples.note: Group 2: 起きる → 起きろ. A blunt wake-up call.
Cheering: the imperative is normal and friendly here.

examples.ja: 先生に「静かにしろ」と言われた。
examples.reading: せんせいに「しずかに しろ」と いわれた。
examples.en: I was told "be quiet" by the teacher.
examples.note: Quoting an order: the imperative stays inside the quote.

examples.reading: かじだ！はやく にげろ！
examples.note: Emergencies are one of the few times the imperative is used to strangers.

examples.ja: 道路の標識に「止まれ」と書いてあった。
examples.reading: どうろの ひょうしきに「とまれ」と かいてあった。
examples.note: Signs use the imperative because it is short and clear.

similarGrammar.difference: A softer command used by parents and teachers and in exam instructions. Still not for superiors.
The negative command: 入るな (Don't enter). Same rough level.
The normal polite and casual requests. Use these in daily conversation instead of the imperative.

commonMistakes.right: 少々お待ちください、先生。
commonMistakes.why: The imperative is far too rough for a teacher or customer. Use お〜ください or 〜てください.
Group 2 verbs take ろ. The え-row change is only for Group 1 verbs (飲め, 書け).
来る has the irregular imperative 来い (こい).

usageNotes: In quoted speech the imperative is neutral: 医者に「毎日歩け」と言われた simply reports the instruction.
〜てくれ (手伝ってくれ) is the imperative of くれる and is a rough but common male request among friends.
The literary Group 2 imperative 〜よ (食べよ, せよ) appears in written instructions and exam wording (答えよ).
jlptTips: You are tested on recognising imperatives inside quotes and on signs: 「〜と書いてある」 or 「〜と言われた」 followed by 止まれ / 入れ / 来い.
Conjugation options may mix 来い / 来ろ / 来れ. Only 来い is correct; likewise しろ (or literary せよ) for する.
